source_span: the biggest jump in the 10yr Treasury yield (+15.2bps) since the market turmoil around Liberation Day in April 2025. The main driver was a strong batch of PMIs...which both led to mounting speculation about faster rate hikes
source_chain: Strong flash PMI (58.4) plus firmer oil therefore hawkish repricing of the Fed path (Oct-hike odds 53%->71%, 37bp priced by year-end) therefore a broad Treasury selloff (10Y +15.2bp to a post-2007 high of 5.11%, biggest one-day jump since April 2025; 5Y above 5% for the first time since 2007, worsened by a weak $70bn auction tailing 3.1bp) therefore equities give way despite good growth data (S&P -0.75%, worst day in a month, broad-based ex-energy). Separately, JPM (17539) argues 10Y fair value near 5.5% makes this a buying dip like past yield-driven selloffs (invalidated only if the consumer breaks or AI capex is cut, or reversed to bullish if oil/yields fall); Morgan Stanley (17416) treats a 4.50% 10Y breach as the level where rate sensitivity bites but keeps its 8,000 target, with 7000-7100 as a tactical downside case only if oil climbs further or midterm seasonality bites; BTIG (17474) reads the move as consolidation within an uptrend, invalidated only by a close below ~4.92%.
pulse_chain: Strong flash PMI (58.4 vs 55.3) therefore hawkish repricing (71% Oct-hike odds vs 53% Tuesday, 37bp priced by year-end) therefore yields up across the curve, 10Y to 5.11% (highest since 2007, biggest one-day jump since April 2025), 5Y above 5% on a weak $70bn auction tailing 3.1bp therefore S&P -0.75%, worst day in a month, broad ex-energy. JPM: fair value ~5.5%, past yield-driven dips get bought, buys this one via a broadening trade, stays cautious/neutral because energy won't settle lower, bullish trigger = lower oil/yields, bearish trigger = consumer breaks or AI capex cut. MS: 4.50% is the rate-sensitivity threshold, correlation already negative, still holds 8,000 target, 7000-7100 downside over 3-5 weeks if oil climbs further. BTIG: 10Y consolidating in an uptrend, flips only below ~4.92%.
why: Every figure and invalidation level in the lead theme traces to a specific source claim with the correct bank attribution and the same direction (PMI beat -> hawkish repricing -> yield spike -> equity weakness, with JPM's dip-buy case, MS's resilient-earnings case, and BTIG's technical level each carrying their own real invalidation), so no step is reversed, misattributed, or invented.
